topics.label: Lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the complement system and outlines the scope of the lecture.

topics.label: Foundations and core mechanics of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational concepts, nomenclature conventions, and central C3-driven framework of the complement system.

topics.label: Complement activation pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the upstream recognition pathways that activate complement on target surfaces and achieve the threshold for a cascade.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of activated complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the downstream effector processes triggered to destroy pathogens and stimulate inflammation.

topics.label: Host cell regulation of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how host cells use regulatory proteins to prevent accidental complement activation on self surfaces.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the distinct pathological conditions and infection risks resulting from deficiencies in specific complement components.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion mechanisms and practical applications
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes how pathogens evade complement destruction and how these bacterial evasion factors are utilized in biomedical applications.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer closes the session and previews the next lecture on the adaptive immune system.
